title: 1953 AHSME Problem 15
statement: A circular piece of metal of maximum size is cut out of a square piece and then a square piece of maximum size is cut out of the circular piece. The total amount of metal wasted is:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: \(\dfrac14\) the area of the original square

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
\(\dfrac12\) the area of the original
square

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: \(\dfrac12\) the area of the circular piece

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: \(\dfrac14\) the area of the circular piece

solutions.text:
Let the original square have side \(s.\) The inscribed circle has diameter \(s.\) That diameter is the diagonal of the largest square cut from the circle, so the final square has side \(\frac{s}{\sqrt2}\) and area \(\frac{s^2}{2}.\) The material left after both cuts is this final square, so the total waste is \(s^2-\frac{s^2}{2}=\frac{s^2}{2}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Let the original square have side \(s\)
The final square’s diagonal equals the circle’s diameter, which is \(s\)
